title: Hospitals and First Aid
subtitle: Hospital notices, a broken arm, a first aid course and a paramedic

parts.title: Notices and messages
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: VISITING HOURS: Visitors are welcome between 2 p.m. and 8 p.m. only. No more than two people at a bedside at the same time, please.
EMERGENCY ENTRANCE: Use the side door for accidents only. For ordinary appointments, please go to the main reception on the ground floor.
PHARMACY: Show the paper from your doctor at the window. Medicine is ready thirty minutes after you hand it in, and the queue is shorter before noon.
FIRST AID COURSE: Learn how to help someone who is hurt. Saturday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. in Room 5. Lunch is not provided, so bring your own food.
HAND WASHING: Please clean your hands with the gel before you enter and after you leave every ward. This protects patients and staff.

parts.title: Health services
parts.instructions: Read what each person is looking for. Match each person to the best text. There are three extra texts.

people.text: Hugh has a toothache that has lasted for two days. He cannot eat properly and wants someone to look at it as soon as possible.
Nadia has hurt her ankle playing hockey. It is swollen and she thinks it might be broken, so she needs a picture of the inside of her foot.

texts.title: Dental Clinic
texts.text: Emergency appointments for toothache and broken teeth. Phone before nine to get a place the same day.

parts.title: A night in hospital
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Last winter, I broke my arm while skating on a frozen lake. At first, I thought it was only a bad bruise, but when my friend Pia tried to lift my hand, I almost shouted with pain. She called an ambulance, and a few minutes later, two paramedics arrived. They were kind and calm, and one of them made a joke that made me laugh.

At the hospital, I had to wait for three hours in a crowded room. A boy with a cut on his head was crying, and an old man next to me was coughing loudly. Finally, a nurse called my name and took me to have an X-ray.

The doctor showed me the picture and said that the bone had broken in two places. I would need a plaster for six weeks. I was disappointed, because I had planned to go skiing in February. 'There will be other winters,' said the doctor, smiling.

I went home at midnight with a blue plaster, and my classmates drew funny pictures on it the next day. Now it is off, and my arm is as good as new. I have promised myself, though, that I will never skate on a lake again without checking how thick the ice is.

questions.prompt: What did the writer first think about the injury?
options: That it was only a bruise
That it was a very serious break
That it would heal by itself
questions.explanation: He thought it was only a bad bruise.

questions.prompt: What did one of the paramedics do?
options: He made a joke to cheer the writer up
He gave the writer a pain killer
He told the writer to stand up
questions.explanation: One made a joke that made him laugh.

questions.prompt: What was unpleasant about the waiting room?
options: It was cold and had no chairs at all
It was crowded and noisy for three hours
It was far from the X-ray department
questions.explanation: He waited three hours in a crowded room.

questions.prompt: Why was the writer disappointed?
options: He had to miss his exams at school
He had to stay in hospital for weeks
He could not go skiing in February
questions.explanation: He had planned to go skiing in February.

questions.prompt: What has the writer decided?
options: To take a first aid course next winter
To stop skating for the rest of his life
To check the ice before skating
questions.explanation: He will check how thick the ice is.

parts.title: Learning first aid
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Last month, I joined a first aid course at the local hospital. I had never done anything like it before, but my mother thought it was a useful skill to learn. [1] We were divided into groups of six, and each group had a different teacher.

Our teacher was a nurse called Mrs Dale, who had worked in hospitals for twenty years. [2] She showed us how to stop bleeding from a cut and how to put a bandage on a hurt knee.

The most difficult part was learning what to do when someone stops breathing. [3] We practised on a plastic model, pressing on its chest again and again until our arms were tired.

At the end of the day, we took a short test. [4] I was very proud of myself when I received my certificate. [5] Now, whenever I see an accident in a film, I know exactly what I would do.
sentences: About thirty people had come, from teenagers to grandparents.
She had a loud voice and a great sense of humour.
It is important to stay calm and call for an ambulance first.
Luckily, I answered nearly all the questions correctly.
The course was held in a large room on the second floor.
It is a day that I will remember for a very long time.

gaps.explanation: About thirty people explains why they were divided into groups.
The teacher is described, and then she showed them first aid actions.
Calling an ambulance is the key step when someone stops breathing, and then they practised.
Answering the questions is about the test, and then he is proud of the certificate.
A day to remember closes the text, followed by the film comment.

parts.title: Staying healthy

parts.passage: Doctors say that it is easy to stay healthy if you follow a few simple rules. You should eat fruit and vegetables [1] day, and you should drink plenty of water. It is also important to take some exercise, [2] walking to school or playing a sport with friends. Try to sleep for at least eight hours [3] night. If you feel ill, you should go to see a doctor [4] soon as possible. Do not wait until the problem becomes serious. Finally, remember [5] wash your hands often, especially before meals. parts.title: A talk about the hospital
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note with one word.

turns.speaker: donna
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to St Mary's Hospital. I'm Donna, one of the nurses. First, a few facts. The hospital opened in nineteen fifty-two, and today more than two thousand people work here. We have six hundred beds. The busiest department is Emergency, which treats about three hundred patients every day. The children's ward is on the third floor, and it has a playroom with books and toys. There is a garden on the roof where patients can sit in good weather. The café opens at seven and closes at five. We also have a small shop that sells flowers and magazines. If you want to become a volunteer, you must be at least sixteen years old. Please ask at reception for a form.

gaps.prompt: The hospital opened in nineteen fifty-___
gaps.explanation: The hospital opened in nineteen fifty-two.

gaps.prompt: Emergency treats about ___ patients every day
gaps.explanation: About three hundred patients every day.

gaps.prompt: The children's ward is on the ___ floor
gaps.explanation: The children's ward is on the third floor.
The café opens at seven and closes at five.

gaps.prompt: Volunteers must be at least ___ years old
gaps.explanation: You must be at least sixteen.

parts.title: A paramedic
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Today I'm talking to Jenna Reed, a paramedic. Jenna, what does a normal day look like?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: There isn't one. One hour, I'm helping someone with a cut finger, and the next, I'm at a serious road accident.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: How long did your training take?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Three years at university, and then six months with an experienced partner. I learned something new every day.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What is the most difficult part of the job?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Staying calm when other people are frightened. If I panic, the patient will panic too.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Do you ever feel sad?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Sometimes, yes, when we cannot save someone. But then I remember all the people we have helped.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: What do you do to relax after a hard day?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: I walk my dog on the beach. It clears my head, and the dog doesn't ask me any questions.

turns.speaker: gerard
turns.text: Would you recommend this job?

turns.speaker: jenna
turns.text: Definitely, if you like people and can work in a team. It is hard work, but it's the best job in the world.
